title: Privacy, worth doing soon: reminders keep arriving that the screen says are off; the email's unsubscribe link is the person's only way out
evidence: PR 1 held (2221, 2026-11-27): health-core merges the opt-in per token (packages/health-core/src/reminder-rows.ts: rowsOf, mergeOptIn, shownOptIn; merge.ts calls mergeOptIn), migrate validates and sanitizes the nested rows, a file with tokens rows is stamped at least version 2, the check after a save covers the opt-in, and setReminderRow (state-edits.ts) is in place for PR 2 (US-17 AC19, US-32 AC67). PR 2 not started; its list: (a) the erase teardown collects active rows from its first read and every adoption until the commit, sparing tokens still active in the standing record; the erase teardown re-reads rowsOf(getReminderOptIn()) at commit, since row-only changes are adopted silently; (b) visibleContentOf compares shownOptIn or the full row set once the control reads rows, and the hidden-rows announce test is inverted; (c) every writer changes together: the switch writes the old token cancelled in the same guarded edit, Turn on keeps rows, Turn off cancels every token; (d) the reminder_optout event maps provider through REMINDER_PROVIDERS; (e) erase.ts strips tokens in its provider tie-break; also the erase adoption and prepare over rows (US-11 AC15). Design: docs/drafts/r9-optin-cancel-merge-design.md. Root fix R9 (triage 2026-11-25): opt-in merge: a cancel beats an active opt-in only for its own token. Residual of H18e (US-17 AC17 Limit). Device A taps Turn off on active T1 while device B turns reminders on (Drive: A's cancel deletes the row, B inserts T2 and writes active T2). If A has not merged B's write before its own (the usual case: the 60 s poll, REMOTE_POLL_MS, packages/health-core/src/record-session.ts:38), A's cancelled T1 carries the later stamp and wins the opt-in merge (pickNewerOptional, packages/health-core/src/merge.ts:389, applied at :856; time first then lamport, cmpClock :423-427). End: the record says cancelled T1 on every device, the server row T2 stays live, pushes stop, and no Turn off in the app reaches T2. The fix is merge-level: a cancel beats an active opt-in only for its own token. A naive rule is not associative, so devices can diverge: aT2(t1), aT1(t3), cT1(t4) merge to cT1 one way and aT1 the other. Design note with a convergence proof first; merge semantics, health-core, engine release. Source: the H18e design note (Option C).
